stated: Reform UK will protect country sports, stating that they increase investment, aid conservation, and boost rural jobs, communities, and local economies.

source.quote: Protect Country Sports These increase investment and help conservation of our environment. They boost rural jobs, communities and local economies.

bearing_set.reason: Policy explicitly claims to boost rural jobs and local economies through country sports, which directly bears on employment quality and security in rural labour markets.

Policy claims conservation benefits from country sports, but the environmental impacts (e.g. driven grouse moor management on peat bogs, lead shot contamination, predator control on biodiversity) are genuinely contested, earning a real verdict on the clean environment fundamental.

The policy asserts increased investment and boosted local rural economies — a plausible aggregate living-standards and economic-activity effect in rural areas, distinct from the distributional job-quality claim on O4.

membership_note: Three distinct mechanisms each earn a non-negligible verdict: rural employment (O4), contested conservation vs environmental harm (O6), and broader rural economic investment and living standards (O13). O10 (personal liberty) was considered — the policy implicitly protects freedom to engage in these activities — but as a maintenance of status quo rather than a change in liberty position, the effect is insufficiently directional to clear the non-negligible bar.
